Let the bipartition be \(L\sqcup R\), with \(|L|=|R|=6\). Encode an orientation by a \(6\times 6\) matrix \(M\), where
\[
M_{ij}=1
\]
means the edge from \(L_i\) to \(R_j\) is oriented \(L_i\to R_j\). A vertex in \(L\) is Eulerian iff its row sum is \(3\). A vertex in \(R\) is Eulerian iff its column sum is \(3\). So we must count \(6\times 6\) zero-one matrices with all row and column sums equal to \(3\).

Group the six rows into three ordered pairs. For one pair of rows, the column-sum vector has entries \(0,1,2\), total \(6\). Its possible sorted types are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{type} & \text{number of such vectors} & \text{row-pair multiplicity}\\
\hline
(1,1,1,1,1,1) & 1 & 20\\
(0,1,1,1,1,2) & 30 & 6\\
(0,0,1,1,2,2) & 90 & 2\\
(0,0,0,2,2,2) & 20 & 1
\end{array}
\]

For example, type \((0,1,1,1,1,2)\) means the two rows share one column, avoid one column, and split the remaining four columns as two-and-two, giving \(\binom42=6\) ordered row pairs.

Fix the third row-pair vector \(c\). The first two row-pair vectors must sum to \(3-c\). A direct finite count gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{type of }c & \text{weighted number for first two row-pairs}\\
\hline
(1,1,1,1,1,1) & 1860\\
(0,1,1,1,1,2) & 936\\
(0,0,1,1,2,2) & 480\\
(0,0,0,2,2,2) & 256
\end{array}
\]

Thus the total number is

\[
20\cdot 1860
+180\cdot 936
+180\cdot 480
+20\cdot 256.
\]

Compute:

\[
37200+168480+86400+5120=297200.
\]

Therefore the exact number of Eulerian orientations of \(K_{6,6}\) is

\[
\boxed{297200}.
\]
